{"prompt":[{"role":"system","content":"You write the notes of a call between a game team and its curator on
GDHub. The team reads them to remember what was said and agreed.

Retell neutrally ("The loop was shown…", "It was agreed…"). Nobody is
named and no speaker is attributed: the transcript cannot tell voices
apart, and a wrong name is worse than none.

The short summary on calls 2–5 is the verdict on the sprint that just
ended, drawn from the whole conversation; the per-task notes carry the
detail.

Write only what was said on the call. The plan, the devlog and the
artifacts are context to recognise what people refer to, not things
to report. Use only task ids from the plan. The transcript is
machine-made and has errors: read through them, do not quote them.
Plain English, short sentences, no filler."},{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Call 1: it sets the plan for the checkpoint.

Goal: A playable vertical slice: two islands, the tide loop and co-op sailing, tested by five players

Plan tasks:




No devlog for the sprint.



Transcript:
Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Let's start with the goal for these four weeks. You want a playable vertical slice: two islands, the tide loop and co-op sailing, tested by five players.
That's right. We have the tide loop working on one island, and the boat moves, but co-op is not in yet.
Then I'd keep the second island out of this sprint. Get one island fully playable with two players sailing together first.
Okay. So the first task is the co-op boat on one island, two players at the same time.
Yes, and record a short video of it at the end of the sprint so I can see it, not just read about it.
The second task we had was the trailer storyboard. Is that still worth it now?
Not this month. A trailer before the slice plays is effort spent on the wrong thing. Cut it, or move it to the next checkpoint.
Fine, we cut it. The third task is the playtest with five players.
Plan it for the last week, after the slice is stable, and write down what each player got stuck on. Those notes are the evidence that the goal is met.
And the build, should we share it?
Yes, share a build anyone on the team can open, with a link that works without logging in. Attach it to the task when you have it.
Agreed. So for this sprint: the co-op boat on one island, a video of it, and a shareable build. Playtest in sprint four.
That's the plan. Next call I'd like to see the boat with two players. Good luck, and post a devlog when the boat works."}]}],"responseFormat":{"type":"json","schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"inShort":{"type":"string","description":"Two or three sentences.
